name: Textile & Apparel
summary: Pakistan’s largest manufacturing-export ecosystem, spanning cotton, spinning, weaving, processing, home textiles and garments.
history: Textiles developed into a core industrial base after independence, expanding from cotton ginning and spinning into integrated value-added apparel and home-textile production. The Ministry of Commerce describes a self-reliant chain from ginning and spinning through weaving, knitting, processing and finished products.
work: Transforms cotton and man-made fibres into yarn, fabric, processed textile, garments, towels, denim, knitwear, home linen and technical textiles.
source: Ministry of Commerce — Textile Wing / Year Book 2024–25

name: Cement
summary: A capital-intensive manufacturing industry supplying cement for housing, infrastructure and commercial construction.
history: Pakistan’s cement capacity expanded over successive industrial-development phases as urbanization, housing and infrastructure increased demand. Producers are organized around integrated plants using limestone and other minerals.
work: Quarries and prepares raw materials, produces clinker in high-temperature kilns, grinds it with additives, then packages or dispatches bulk cement.

name: Automotive & Engineering
summary: Vehicle assembly, tractors, motorcycles, components and engineering supply chains supported by localization and industrial policy.
history: Pakistan has used successive auto-development policies to encourage local assembly, parts manufacturing, localization and exports. The Ministry of Industries lists Auto Industry Development and Export Policy 2021–26 and the newer New Energy Vehicles Policy 2025–30 among current policy frameworks.
work: Combines component manufacturing, stamping, machining, painting, assembly, testing, dealerships and after-sales services.

name: Pharmaceuticals
summary: A regulated healthcare manufacturing sector covering medicines, biological products and related therapeutic goods.
history: Modern pharmaceutical manufacturing in Pakistan operates under a national regulatory framework. DRAP, established under the DRAP Act 2012, coordinates and enforces requirements for therapeutic goods and oversees licensing, registration, surveillance and quality functions.
work: Formulation, manufacturing, quality control, packaging, registration, pharmacovigilance and distribution of therapeutic products.

name: Energy & Power
summary: Power generation, transmission and distribution plus petroleum, gas, coal and renewable-energy systems.
history: Pakistan’s energy system has evolved from conventional thermal and hydropower toward a broader mix that includes nuclear, wind, solar and other sources. The Pakistan Economic Survey tracks installed electricity capacity, generation and energy consumption as national indicators.
work: Generates electricity, moves it through transmission networks, distributes it to consumers, and manages fuel and renewable-energy supply chains.

name: Steel & Metals
summary: A foundational materials industry supporting construction, engineering, transport, appliances and infrastructure.
history: Steel production and re-rolling grew alongside Pakistan’s construction and engineering sectors. The sector includes integrated and mini-mill production, scrap-based melting, re-rolling and downstream fabrication.
work: Melts or processes iron and steel inputs into billets, bars, sheets, coils and fabricated products used by other industries.

name: Fertilizer & Chemicals
summary: Process industries supplying agricultural nutrients and industrial chemicals to the wider economy.
history: Fertilizer development has been closely linked with Pakistan’s agricultural productivity and natural-gas-based industrialization. Government industrial policy has long included fertilizer-sector frameworks.
work: Uses chemical processing to manufacture nitrogenous and other fertilizers, with associated storage, bagging, logistics and dealer networks.
source: Ministry of Industries & Production — Industrial Policies

name: Food & Agro Processing
summary: Turns agricultural output into packaged foods, beverages, dairy, edible oils, milling and other consumer products.
history: Food processing grew with Pakistan’s large agricultural base, urbanization and modern retail. It connects farms to industrial processing, cold chains, packaging and consumer markets.
work: Procures crops, milk, livestock and other inputs; processes, tests, packages and distributes food products.

name: IT & Digital Services
summary: Software, IT-enabled services, cloud, freelancing and digital-product activity serving domestic and international markets.
history: Pakistan’s technology-services ecosystem expanded with internet adoption, software exports, freelancing and startup growth. Public institutions track IT and telecom as a distinct part of the economy.
work: Builds software, digital platforms, IT-enabled business services, cloud solutions, cybersecurity and data/AI products.
source: Pakistan Economic Survey — Information Technology & Telecommunication
